counterfactual_missing_items: No normal troponin or resolved ECG changes that would refute acute MI
No normal wall motion on echocardiography
No non-obstructive coronary anatomy on angiography
decisive_items: Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
response.rationale: R2 integrates the strongest multi-modal raw evidence: acute chest pain, elevated troponin, anterior wall hypomotility, and a proximal LAD culprit stenosis, matching an acute MI. R6 is a broader valid syndrome but is less specific because it also includes unstable angina; R3 and R5 rest on partial ECG excerpts (aVR ST elevation vs precordial ST/T changes) and do not incorporate the troponin and imaging confirmation.

rejected.why: Chronic CAD label only captures the angiography finding and misses the acute syndrome, troponin elevation, and wall-motion abnormality.
The aVR ST elevation and reciprocal inferior depression are suggestive but not sufficient for STEMI, and it omits troponin, anterior hypomotility, and LAD stenosis.
NSTEMI label relies on nonspecific ST depression/T-wave changes and misses the aVR ST elevation and tall T waves suggestive of proximal LAD occlusion, plus troponin and imaging.
Hypertension and elevated BP are risk factors rather than the acute diagnosis; it ignores troponin, ECG, echocardiography, and angiography.
Append-only completion of R6; adds troponin but remains broad ACS and lacks echo/coronary imaging localization.
Append-only completion of R1; adds proximal LAD anatomy but still labels chronic CAD rather than acute MI.
Append-only completion of R2; anterior hypomotility is a localizing consequence, but this single-span completion cannot independently establish MI.
